topic: rare-signal detection with false alarms, censoring, heralding, and calibrated nuisance
overall_status: internally_derived_classical_components; no novelty or external-validation claim

claims.statement: For a binary sequential detector with hypothesis-independent adaptive action and censoring kernels, per-action costs c(a)>0, and finite κ_h=sup_a D(P_h^a||P_(1-h)^a)/c(a), type-I error <= alpha and type-II error <= beta imply κ_1 E_1[C] >= d(1-beta||alpha) and κ_0 E_0[C] >= d(1-alpha||beta).
assumptions: The full stopped transcript, including action, calibration, herald/failure, censoring, and stopping records, is modeled under both hypotheses.
Action-selection and censoring kernels are the same functions of observed history under either hypothesis.
Costs are charged for every attempted measurement, preparation, calibration, control, and readout that the chosen scalar cost includes.
Divergences may be infinite; if so that direction gives no finite lower bound.
claims.status: proof reconstructed directly from KL chain rule and binary data processing; classic ingredients; not a novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Stopped KL inequalities and SPRT optimality are classical. The contribution is explicit charging and scope bookkeeping across adaptive censoring, calibration, and postselection.
claims.costs: Expected total action cost under the named hypothesis. A mean-cost promise does not imply hard spectral support or total thermodynamic cost unless those are explicitly included.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the chain-rule inequality under the stated common action/censoring kernels, or a policy meeting both errors while exceeding the derived bound assumptions without adding information/cost to the transcript.
claims.next_gate: Instantiate the lemma for a measured channel with a complete action/resource vector and compare its attainable KL-per-cost frontier against the strongest policy with the same calibration information.

claims.statement: For fixed exposure T and known b>0,s>0, the randomized upper-count threshold is most powerful at size alpha for Pois(bT) versus Pois((b+s)T); the KL rates per exposure are I1=(b+s)ln(1+s/b)-s and I0=s-b ln(1+s/b), and every test with size alpha and miss beta satisfies T I1>=d(1-beta||alpha), T I0>=d(1-alpha||beta).
assumptions: A homogeneous Poisson background and additive homogeneous signal rate hold over the full exposure.
The background rate and signal rate are known inputs; background calibration cost is not included unless separately charged.
All event counts used by the likelihood are retained.
claims.status: formula derived; known-background threshold/power computed to finite floating-point precision, on/off power reports an explicit tail bound; primary statistical method is classical
claims.novelty_boundary: Neyman-Pearson testing and Poisson signal-background inference predate this work; no new detector or asymptotic exponent is claimed.
claims.costs: Exposure T, with added terms for probe energy, instrument, calibration, control, and computation required by the actual deployment.
claims.falsifier: Observed counts fail the specified Poisson law, b or s are not calibrated/stationary, or the computed randomized threshold does not attain its null size and Neyman-Pearson power for the specified pair.
claims.next_gate: Validate against independent null and signal runs, retaining all marks and charging calibration exposure; include the calibration cost before comparing with a known-b baseline.

claims.statement: For on-count-only observations with unknown background b in an interval of width at least s, the null family Pois(Tb) and signal family Pois(T(b+s)) contain an identical pair of laws. Any uniformly size-alpha test then has power <=alpha at that alternative, so alpha+beta>=1.
assumptions: The only observed data are counts in the signal/on region.
The same background interval is allowed under both hypotheses and its width is at least the signal-rate increment s.
Uniform type-I control is required over the entire null nuisance family.
claims.status: elementary exact impossibility proof; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a direct identifiability obstruction, not a new statistical theorem.
claims.costs: It applies even with unlimited repetitions of the same on-only experiment because the two hypotheses can induce identical laws at every exposure.
claims.falsifier: A valid extra observable or calibration assumption that separates the two distributions; this changes the model and removes the premise.
claims.next_gate: Specify a background-only reference or validated bounded drift/transfer model, then charge its exposure and re-run a uniform-power analysis.

claims.statement: For one attempt with herald probability q_h and conditional success-output law R_h, if the success/failure flag is recorded then D(P1||P0)=d(q1||q0)+q1 D(R1||R0). Repeating physical attempts until a herald succeeds costs c/q_h in expectation under H_h.
assumptions: The attempt outcome is failure with probability 1-q_h or success with probability q_h followed by an output drawn from R_h.
Each attempt costs c, including failed attempts.
When conditioning on success, the success-rate term is omitted from the conditional-output statistic but not from physical exposure.
claims.novelty_boundary: This accounting identity does not invalidate a computational conditional sampler; it distinguishes algorithmic sampling of a conditional law from physical herald preparation.
claims.costs: All failed attempts, conditional-output processing, positive-kernel/model acquisition, representation bits, random bits, and sampler runtime are separate line items.
claims.falsifier: A heralding protocol whose actual one-attempt record law does not factor as the specified success flag and conditional output; update the model to the true outcome space.
claims.next_gate: For any claimed inverse-success-free conditional sampler, independently verify exact zero-event detection, relative rather than additive counting, input representation acquisition, bit complexity, and physical-versus-computational interpretation.
